title: You don’t wrestle with this question unless something in you already knows what it feels like to drift.
paragraphs: You don’t wrestle with this question unless something in you already knows what it feels like to drift.
To be chosen… and still compromise.
To be called… and still fall.
That’s where the story of Samson cuts deeper than most people are willing to admit.
Because his life refuses to stay in a neat category.
Before there was strength in his arms, there was a word over his life.
Before the victories… before the women… before the collapse…
In Book of Judges 13, an angel announces that this child would be set apart. A Nazirite from birth. No razor. No compromise. A life consecrated to God.
“But here’s what most people don’t realize…”
You watch him grow into power.
Lions torn apart with bare hands.
Moments where the Spirit of the Lord rushes upon him.
He keeps walking toward what God warned him about.
And you feel it, don’t you?
Because it’s possible to be used by God publicly…
He touches what he wasn’t supposed to touch.
He wants what he wasn’t supposed to want.
He keeps stepping closer to the edge, like the calling will protect him from consequence.
A test he keeps failing… slowly.
“And she made him sleep on her knees…” (Judges 16:19)
That’s what happens when conviction fades.
Then the line that should shake you:
“He did not know that the Lord had left him.” (Judges 16:20)
He still thought he was strong.
Still thought he could shake himself free.
That’s what silent drift looks like.
You don’t feel it at first.
The man who once shook nations… reduced to chains.
So now the question burns harder:
Did he throw it all away?
“O Lord God, remember me, I pray! Strengthen me, I pray, just this once…” (Judges 16:28)
“The dead that he killed at his death were more than he had killed in his life.” (Judges 16:30)
More in his death… than his life.
So did he waste his calling?
He nearly destroyed himself along the way.
But God still accomplished His purpose through a broken man who finally turned back.
That’s the part you weren’t expecting.
Because you thought calling required perfection.
And Samson waited too long to fully give it.
Because you’re not reading this by accident.
You’ve told yourself you still have time.
You’ve assumed you can always “shake yourself free” later.
But what if you’re closer to that moment than you think?
What if you’re already drifting and don’t feel it?
Here’s the truth Samson’s life screams without saying it cleanly:
Sin will take you further than you planned.
Keep you longer than you wanted.
Cost you more than you expected.
Grace still answers the one who truly turns back.
And this is where Jesus stands greater than Samson.
Because Samson’s final act brought temporary deliverance.
But Jesus Christ didn’t just die among His enemies…
“For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son…” (John 3:16)
Where Samson’s strength destroyed a building…
Where Samson’s death ended his story…
So don’t ask this question from a distance.
Are you wasting what God has given you?
Or are you finally going to surrender it?
Because there are only two directions from here:
Keep drifting… and lose more than you think.
Or turn now… while your story is still being written.
Someone you know is walking the same edge Samson walked.
Stay if you want Scripture that confronts, not comforts deception.
And if you’re ready to go deeper, where conviction turns into transformation, step into that next level here:
Because this isn’t just about Samson.
It’s about what you’re going to do next.
